title: Bind P112 tetrad decoder to selected ports; no kappa change
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This package binds the existing P112 tetrad-local masked decoder to the selected complex provider's 112 nine-bit ports. An explicit bijection preserves all 12,544 pairings; transporting the 14 tetrads verifies 6,720 constrained entries and gives 56 rank-2 terms with total copy charge 112.

It then screens a conditional two-sided rank-32 budget. With the selected 192 phase units, centre charge 112, 166 ideal complex rank-32 children, and two hypothetical unpaid coordinates, the complex moment at `a=1/99` is `0.996649697627`, with ideal κ cap `0.0137876681081`. The bit-side profile (nine rank-7 copies and 158 rank-32 children, inherited surcharge retained) has ideal cap `0.0319843333739`; the joint ideal cap is `0.0137876681081`. Both one-unpaid controls fail.

This is a source-bound coefficient identity and a planning relaxation, not a physical construction or selected-κ improvement. The new terms lack a dirty-input implementation, source/restoration/consumer invoice, and owner chronology; both two-unpaid endpoint contracts remain assumptions. The selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

Task card `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, priority revision 6; scope changed from finding and fully pricing a new child-rank shape to binding the exact P112 decoder to selected ports and screening its conditional ideal budget. The package records the change in `research/selected-p112-tetrad-rank32-route/TASK.json`; base commit is `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, with source inputs pinned in `SOURCES.json`.

The nearest adjacent budget direction is [PR #3344](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3344), which studies larger children and multiple unpaid coordinates. Open [PR #3567](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3567) screens the effective rank and term cap of a one-sided tetrad-local alphabet; it does not bind this decoder to selected ports. Open [PR #3604](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3604) uses the selected P112 basis for coefficient fusion and derives a conditional inverse-transpose map for all fourteen centre-cut blocks. It also shows that coefficient fusion leaves the dirty baseline unchanged; using the map needs a full basis transform or a separately available 281-coefficient correction, neither of which is source-admitted yet. That follow-up relies on the selected-port binding here, but neither PR proves the complete physical endpoint or the two-unpaid coverage law. The P112 local decoder predecessor establishes the local 112-copy floor but not this selected-port binding. The cached overlap scan covers 394 open PRs and 2,319 discussions as of 2026-10-18 03:15 UTC; refresh failed, so it is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

Replayed with Python 3.12 using standard-library-only inputs:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-p112-tetrad-rank32-route/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-p112-tetrad-rank32-route --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-p112-tetrad-rank32-route
```

The verifier reconstructs the selected word and P112 geometry, checks the explicit port bijection over all 12,544 pairs, verifies all 6,720 constrained entries and the rank of each of the 56 terms, and recomputes both sides' interval-priced profiles. The one-unpaid controls fail. A full physical supplier, changed endpoint contracts, and selected cold-construction replay are not claimed.

## Credit

The P112 geometry and local identity retain the attribution in `research/p112-tetrad-local-decoder/`; the selected source archive, complex ceiling, centre ledger and bit pricing engine retain the pins and licenses in this package's `SOURCES.json`. Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No independent human review is claimed; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can the 56 mapped rank-2 terms be compiled into a dirty-input endpoint within the rank-32 budget? Implement one eight-port tetrad block first and record source access, frame, restoration and consumer costs. PR #3604 supplies the conditional map and a separate dirty-baseline correction, but there is still no source-bound dirty-input channel, chronological provider interface, or complete invoice for the new terms.
2. Can both suppliers justify two unpaid coordinates while retaining their rank-32 profiles? Trace each actual data endpoint and replay a complete dirty-input instance before assigning the changed coverage law. The selected contracts currently certify only one unpaid coordinate.
